questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me that it was a destination, that I was exited to learn more about, that the University offerered some courses that I was interested in, and that I could see myself living in the country for five months.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of information through email form Erasmus University of Rotterdam, which made it easy to know what I had to prepare before and during my arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of email from the University specifying where to meet the first days and what to expect from the first days of my exchange.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It war extremely difficult, even though I started to look four months before my arrival. I tried a lot of different housing sites and Facebook groups, where I unfortunately discovered a lot of scammers.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Start your searching almost the second you get into the University, be aware of scammers and be prepared to live at hostels or airbnbs in the beginning.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to follow six courses during my exchange, which is a lot more than I am use to from my home University. I also had to fill in my second priorities, which made it a total of 12 different courses. I did not get all of my priorities and had to do a second round. It took a lot of research and I had orientate my a lot in the course catalogue, despite this I think the registration process was well structured and organized.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I received an email with guidance from Erasmus University of Rotterdam

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get all of my priorities and had to do a second round.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you read the course descriptions from all the courses that you apply for. Some of the course titels are a bit tricky and misleading.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was very different from course to course. In total I was satisfied with the level. I also took some courses that is very different from my studies, which of course made the level more challenging.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different that I had to follow six courses in one semester, which to some degree made the learning experience more shallow.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- International and Global Communication
- Media and Communications Theory
- Aesthetics
- Feeling Orange
- International Journalism
- Values of Culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International and Global Communication, was a really interesting course, including captivating lectures and a lot of knowledge that was contextualized.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My bike got stolen.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was pretty much as I had expected and very similar to til prizes in Denmark. Of course I was surprised about all the expenses concerning my personal spending. Be prepared to use a lot of money on events and travels.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I bought the Sports Pass, which gave me access to follow a lot different classes, and membership to the running club. ESN also arranged a lot of fun activities both during day and night. The Rotterdam Pass is also available, but I do not know if it was available trough the institution specifically.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Join a sports club. It is super fun and give you inside in other groups.
Go to some of the events arranged by ESN and ENO.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on a lot of day trips to different cities in The Netherlands or other countries. The Netherland has a perfect location and it is easy to take the train to a lot of exiting destinations.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. The school and the city is very international and the culture is kind of similar to Danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I was so lucky that I already had a Dutch friend, which gave me a lot of insight and local friends. If you do not no anyone beforehand I think it would be very difficult and you might have to be satisfied with making friends among the other exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did nit find anything particularly challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Remember to go on fun day trips to different locations.
- Join a sports club or the activities arranged by the University associations.
- Look for housing immediatly!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the great experiences I had and all the fantastic people that I got to know.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To find housing and moving from place to place.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
